rationale: All 3 lenses ran to completion (blind, edge-case, acceptance) against a real spec. Two independently-corroborated major findings survive triage: a third existing User(...) construction site (EnterpriseIdpWrapper.authenticate) was never updated to populate default_project, silently breaking AC2/4/8 for that auth path; and switching current_project's no-default fallback from list/DB order to sorted() causes a one-time silent billing-attribution shift for pre-existing multi-project users at deploy (migration is additive-only, no backfill). Several other blind-lens concerns (stale is_default rows, probe-function divergence, current_project sort as a deploy change in principle) were investigated and refuted or found to be already-accepted, documented tradeoffs by the edge-case lens with concrete evidence (DB partial unique index, default_project always a subset of project_names, no divergence in the two budget-scope probes) - 5 findings dismissed, 0 deferred.

findings.title: EnterpriseIdpWrapper.authenticate() never populates default_project
findings.problem: EnterpriseIdpWrapper.authenticate() (Keycloak/OIDC enterprise auth) builds a security.User by copying every field 1:1 from idp_user (project_names, admin_project_names, roles, etc.) but has no default_project= argument, so it always defaults to None regardless of DB state.
findings.impact: AC2, AC4, and AC8 silently fail for any user authenticated through the enterprise IDP wrapper: their default project is never consulted by _resolve_effective_project's is_global branch, User.current_project, or the CLI proxy's _extract_request_info - they keep being charged personal budget / an arbitrary project exactly as before this ticket, with no error or indication.
findings.recommendation: Add default_project=getattr(idp_user, 'default_project', None) (matching the existing defensive getattr pattern already used for client_access_token two lines below, for forward-compat with the external codemie_enterprise package) if idp_user can carry it; otherwise derive it the same way as the other two sites, from whatever project-membership data this wrapper already has access to. Extend tests/enterprise/idp/test_enterprise_idp_wrapper.py with a default_project case.

findings.title: Switching current_project's fallback to sorted() silently reassigns billing for existing multi-project users at deploy
findings.problem: EPMCDME-15110's migration is additive-only with no backfill (every existing UserProject row starts is_default=false). This diff changes current_project's no-default fallback from self.project_names (original DB/list order) to sorted(self.project_names). For any existing user with 2+ projects and no explicit default (i.e. everyone, until they set one), current_project immediately picks whichever project sorts alphabetically first instead of whatever it resolved to before this deploy.
findings.impact: current_project feeds set_llm_context(None, user.current_project, user) at 9 call sites (assistant.py, workflow.py, workflow_executions.py, skill.py), so this can silently misattribute LLM usage/billing to a different project than before the deploy, for the entire pre-existing multi-project user population, with zero logging or opt-in. This is a real production side effect of fixing AC5's determinism requirement, not a bug in the determinism logic itself.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) ship a data migration/backfill that sets is_default=true on each existing multi-project user's current first-by-original-order project before this code deploys, so the visible project doesn't change for anyone at rollout, or (b) explicitly document and accept this one-time reassignment in the MR description / release notes as a known, intentional side effect of making project selection deterministic, so reviewers and on-call are not surprised by it. Either way this needs an explicit decision, not a silent code change.
